answer: Structural PR-ONLY guard is live. Every enumerated publishing entry point (publish, list_remote, expose, yank, deprecate, revoke, promote) returns BLOCKED-NEEDS-OWNER under the binding PR-ONLY config and never reaches the unique sink _outbound_publish. The same path proceeds under a PUBLIC_MARKETPLACE fixture, so the guard is mode-driven and not a stub. An AST audit of tools/marketplace (tests excluded) finds zero outbound-publish-capable calls outside pr_only_guard.py; a planted urllib.request.urlopen bypass is detected and the auditor is silent after removal. question_or_target: Implement a hard guard that refuses any operation that would publish, list, or expose a package outside the local/private boundary while release mode is PR-ONLY, emitting an owner-approval request instead.

residuals.claim: _outbound_publish is importable from outside tools/marketplace because it is a Python function, not an OS sandbox.
IMP-0111 (governance policy) and IMP-0071 (channels) are not present in this worktree. This unit ships the PR-ONLY chokepoint those units compose onto; it does not pretend those receipts exist.
